health.sacOn: Smart App Control is on. It can block programs and DLL files that are not signed or not yet known to Microsoft, for example PHP extensions or Apache modules. Then a service does not start and Portly names the blocked file. Options: keep it on and use only the versions that start; or turn it off in Windows Security > App & browser control > Smart App Control (Windows cannot turn it back on without a reset). Portly cannot change this setting for you.
health.sacEval: Smart App Control is in evaluation mode. Windows watches which programs you use and may switch it on later; then it can block PHP extensions or Apache modules. If a service suddenly stops starting, Portly names the blocked file. You can turn it off in Windows Security > App & browser control > Smart App Control.
